meta.title: cq-mev: what it reads, writes and sends
meta.facts: Recipe facts from cq-mev's recipe descriptor (#315) at commit e02d949, on main since PRs #345 and #346 (2026-10-03) and not yet in a release; the last release is v0.5.16. Structure and flows compiled from the cq-mev source at main a36449e. Code facts only: no instance data.

packages.name: adobe/mev:cq-mev-connectors
packages.note: Optional. Installs disabled. No key may be configured on any instance until corporate guidance permits it.

bundles.note: The contract only; it can't reach a model

gates.label: Access gate
gates.rule: Both must pass: the helper's marker check with the caller's own session (cq-mev-helper-operators, cq-mev-helper-inference-operators, administrators) AND the instance's Felix Web Console rule (default users = [admin]).

states.example: live heap >= 90 %, GC >= 20 %, instance Sling jobs stalled
states.answer: 409 run_conditions_hot; only an explicit yes runs it

states.example: helper queue suspended or >= 10 jobs; >= 7,500 observation changes

gates.label: One capture at a time
gates.rule: content-architecture, sling-jobs, packages, htl-use-classes and workflow-instances each allow one capture at a time.

gates.label: Exact-payload consent
gates.rule: A hosted question sends nothing before the operator reviews the exact bytes; consent binds requestHash = provider + endpoint + model + body. An uncertain dispatch is never retried.

blocks.label: Console
blocks.summary: /adobe/mev/ui: one static page, vanilla JS, strict CSP, text-only rendering.

blocks.label: Native routes
blocks.summary: 22 exact URI templates. GETs bypass Sling request processing (#170), so pages, pulse and run reads keep answering when Sling fails. POSTs go through Sling.

blocks.label: Access gate
blocks.summary: Every page, API route and the pulse pass Web.authorize.

blocks.label: API v1
blocks.summary: /adobe/mev/api/v1: jobs, recipes, relationships, pulse, purge, inference, settings, content roots and roll-up.

blocks.label: Run conditions
blocks.summary: Don't throw fuel on a hot instance; don't add a capture to a backed-up queue.

blocks.label: Live pulse
blocks.summary: Four tiles, sampled every 5 s while the tab is visible. Stored nowhere; not evidence.

blocks.label: Job service
blocks.summary: Submits captures, consumes them as Sling jobs on one ordered queue, and reconciles every 30 s.

blocks.label: Sealed store
blocks.summary: Seals each snapshot with its SHA-256 in one save; never changes it. Per-recipe folders, newest 100 runs per recipe, a byte budget (#330).

blocks.label: Catalogs
blocks.summary: Deterministic checks over a sealed snapshot. No repository or runtime call.

blocks.label: Diffs
blocks.summary: New since an earlier run, by subject key.

blocks.label: Explain and questions
blocks.summary: Answers from saved graphs without capturing: Explain, local questions, class visibility.

blocks.label: Hosted question
blocks.summary: One reviewed question: five manifest fields of one bundle. Off: no keys.

blocks.label: Connector contract
blocks.summary: Shipped in the helper package; can't reach a model by itself.

blocks.label: Provider connectors
blocks.summary: jev, anthropic, openai. Optional package; installs disabled; no keys.

blocks.label: Settings page
blocks.summary: /adobe/mev/settings: connector key enrollment (administrators; don't) and the read-only instance-role declaration.

blocks.label: Pinned baselines
blocks.summary: Pin a run as the baseline a diff compares against, so purge keeps it (#188).

blocks.label: Scheduled captures
blocks.summary: Weekly around the full-compaction window, under the service user, never during compaction.

blocks.label: Health checks cq-mev-live and cq-mev-evidence
blocks.summary: For a managed-services provider's upstream alerting. OK never means healthy.

recipes.name: OSGi relationships
recipes.question: What is AEM waiting for, and what changed in the OSGi framework since the last graph?
readsFrom: OSGi framework: bundles, wiring and start levels
ConfigurationAdmin: PIDs and change counts only
recipes.cost: The heaviest: about 18 KB of graph per bundle, up to 2,000 bundles, stored gzipped. Memory is checked before capture and before every read
recipes.neverReads: Service objects, configuration values (only PID and change count), raw bundle locations, activation-failure text

recipes.name: HTL Use classes
recipes.question: Can the script class loader load every Java class an HTL script under /apps names?
recipes.neverReads: Script text beyond `data-sly-use` identifiers; never loads a class or renders; `/libs`

recipes.name: Bundle provenance
recipes.question: Who declares this bundle's origin and license?
recipes.neverReads: Anything beyond allowlisted manifest headers; never calls a model, even with hosted inference enabled

recipes.name: Settings & installer
recipes.question: Which reviewed configuration settings differ from safe defaults, and is the OSGi installer alive?
readsFrom: Allowlisted keys of a fixed list of configuration PIDs
OSGi installer registrations and worker threads
recipes.cost: A fixed list of 14 PIDs, plus thread names
recipes.neverReads: Keys outside the allowlist, secrets, the installer's resource list

recipes.name: Selected bundle runtime evidence
recipes.question: What is this one bundle wired to right now?
readsFrom: One bundle's current revision and wiring
recipes.neverReads: Service objects, JARs, configuration, content, installer data

recipes.name: Model publisher suggestion
recipes.question: Which publisher does a hosted model suggest for one bundle, from five reviewed manifest fields?
readsFrom: Five manifest fields of one bundle, from a sealed `bundle-provenance@1` snapshot
recipes.cost: One paid request, after exact-payload review
recipes.neverReads: Everything but five manifest fields of one bundle. **Not usable: no keys**

recipes.name: Repository vitals
recipes.question: Is Oak indexing, checkpointing, collecting garbage and serving queries normally right now?
readsFrom: Allowlisted Oak MBean attributes: indexing lanes, checkpoints, query engine, repository statistics, observation, segment store, caches and sessions
recipes.neverReads: MBean operations, error and log text, index contents, repository content

recipes.name: Index complexity analysis
recipes.question: How complex is this indexing problem, and which path does it need before anyone acts?
readsFrom: Allowlisted Oak async-lane MBean attributes, twice, 15 s apart
recipes.cost: Two JMX samples 15 s apart, so other captures queue behind it
recipes.neverReads: MBean operations (no catch-up, abort or pause); failure traces are reduced to a category in memory, and no message is kept

recipes.name: Blob store
recipes.question: Are blob reads and writes failing, and what DataStore is configured?
readsFrom: Allowlisted blob store and Blob GC MBean attributes
recipes.neverReads: MBean operations, configuration values, binaries, the maintenance history's message text

recipes.name: Scheduler & threads
recipes.question: Is each async lane's scheduled task still registered, and is its thread pool starved or stuck?
recipes.cost: Service properties, pool MBeans, thread names and states
recipes.neverReads: Scheduler or MBean operations, thread stacks, payloads

recipes.name: Replication agents & queues
recipes.question: Is content leaving this author, and if not, which agent or queue is holding it?
readsFrom: Allowlisted replication and distribution agent MBean attributes
recipes.neverReads: `QueueNumEntries` (an unbounded query), queue entries and payloads, agent endpoints and credentials

recipes.name: Persisted Sling jobs
recipes.question: What is waiting under /var/eventing/jobs, and what stinks in it?
readsFrom: Persisted Sling jobs under `/var/eventing/jobs`, by name
recipes.neverReads: Job properties and payloads, `findJobs` or any query, queue actions

recipes.name: Workflow instances
recipes.question: How many workflow instances does this instance keep, in which state and of which model, and does the purge keep up?
recipes.callerSession: Workflow instance trees and the models they name
readsFrom: Workflow instances under `/var/workflow/instances` and `/etc/workflow/instances`, four properties each
recipes.cost: Walks the instance trees, 4 properties each (300,000 nodes, 20 s)

recipes.name: Package store
recipes.question: What does /etc/packages keep, which installs or uninstalls are landmines, and what stinks in it?
recipes.callerSession: `/etc/packages`, and at level 3 the roots its packages name
readsFrom: Level 3: whether each package's roots exist
recipes.cost: You choose: level 1 reads definitions, level 2 adds sizes, level 3 adds up to 10,000 root lookups outside `/etc/packages`
recipes.neverReads: Package binaries, the FileVault API, Package Manager's list, any write

recipes.name: Content architecture (conf + page census)
recipes.question: What /conf and page-template shape does this content root have, and what stinks in it?
readsFrom: One `/content` root: its pages and seven `jcr:content` properties each
recipes.neverReads: Titles, body text, tag values, user identities, queries

sessions.job: Captured inside the Sling job with OSGi/JMX APIs; reads no JCR content.
sessions.caller@submit: Read with the submitting operator's own session at submission and sealed in the request. What the operator can't read looks absent.
sessions.split: One part read with the operator's session at submission and carried into the job; the rest captured in the job.
sessions.sealed at consent: Works only from a sealed snapshot; sealed when the operator consents to the exact payload.

The limits. Read this before acting

steps.text: An operator presses Capture on a card in /adobe/mev/ui.
NativeRoutes hands the POST to Sling and ApiServlet. Web.authorize checks the helper's markers with the caller's own session and the Web Console rule. A plain no is 403 access_denied.
Run conditions read heap, GC time and queues. Hot asks once; backed-up and thrashing refuse with no override.

A recipe sealed at submission reads now, with the operator's own session, and seals its snapshot in the request. Every other recipe is queued as a Sling job on topic com/adobe/mev/helper/assess; three of them (index complexity, blob store, settings) also read one part with the operator's session at submission and carry it into the job.
The ordered queue runs one job at a time. The recipe reads only what its recipe allows, within a fixed budget, and records what it couldn't see.
JobStore seals the snapshot and its SHA-256 in one save under /var/cq-mev-helper/jobs, with the service user. It never changes it.
The catalog assesses the sealed document only. A retry never captures again.
The console polls the run's stage timeline and shows findings: evidence, why, not proven, next check.
Compare shows what is new since an earlier run, by subject key.
A person decides what to do, outside cq-mev. Nothing in cq-mev offers to fix anything.

flows.title: The author got slow after this morning's deploy. Why?

steps.text: Pulse first: is the JVM hot or thrashing, a queue at its load cap, the observation queue backed up, a lane failing? A refused capture is itself the answer to 'how bad is it now'.
osgi-relationships@1, then What's new since the previous graph? Bundles whose version or state changed; services that appeared or disappeared; new stinks.
htl-use-classes@1 if pages render empty: htl-use-class-not-loadable names the script, the line and the class.
index-complexity@1 if the deploy shipped index definitions: pendingReindexes and neverBuilt per lane.
osgi-settings@1 for debug-logging-configured.
What cq-mev can't tell you: it doesn't measure latency or read request, query or error logs. 'Slow' stays unknown; you get evidence about likely causes.

flows.title: Is this package safe to uninstall?

steps.text: Capture packages@1 at level 3 as a user who can read the content roots. A root you can't read looks absent.

Find the package under Landmines: uninstall-reverts-to-first-install, uninstall-deletes-root (critical, proven from creation dates), uninstall-may-delete-root (a size heuristic), install-rewrites-acls.
Read notProven: filter rules can narrow a root, and the snapshot is never opened.
Next check: compare the snapshot with the roots today, on a copy. cq-mev never answers 'safe'.
Async indexing tile: each lane's state. paused is held in memory only; not being run means no run for over 5 minutes.
repository-vitals@1: lane state, bad Lucene indexes, oldest checkpoint, segment-not-found and blob-error counters.
index-complexity@1: grades each lane and failing index L0-L4, with a walk-through. It runs nothing.
scheduler-threads@1 if a lane is not being run: is its task registered, does its pool have a live thread?
sling-jobs@1: job-lookups-on-stale-index shows when job lookups depend on a failing lane.
healthy is a lane state, not a health certificate for the indexes.

houseRules: Read-only to the application: writes only the helper's own records
No added load on a hot instance; no capture onto a backed-up queue
No hidden expensive reads: every recipe has a budget and a never-reads list
Real data stays out of Git
Nothing is sent to a model implicitly

lessons.title: Queued isn't the backlog
lessons.text: Sling counts at most 10 jobs per topic in memory, so a backlog persisted in the repository doesn't show.

lessons.title: Active doesn't mean working
lessons.text: A component can report active after its worker thread has died.

lessons.title: Succeeded doesn't mean compacted
lessons.text: Revision cleanup records a run that skipped compaction as succeeded.

lessons.title: Uninstall isn't undo
lessons.text: FileVault takes a package's snapshot once, at the first install. Uninstall restores that snapshot, and it deletes any filter root that didn't exist back then.

findings: maintenance history: estimated and skipped compaction

direction.title: Captures for trusted, authorized AI agents
statements: Models reason only over the evidence and findings cq-mev has already captured and sealed, and nothing else (#325, design).
No model API key is configured on any instance until corporate guidance permits it.
Nothing is sent implicitly. Every hosted question needs review of the exact payload and consent to it.
Model answers are advice. They are stored apart from the evidence and never replace it.
Health checks for upstream alerting (cq-mev-live, cq-mev-evidence) are designed, not built (#190). OK will never mean healthy.
